page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at top, with the printed page number at the top left. Below the running head, a Greek-and-Latin commentary paragraph. Then a paragraph ending in a Greek passage, a decorative ornament rule, the chapter title "DE IVREIVRANDO.", the subtitle "TITVLVS SEXTVS.", and a closing paragraph opening with a large initial. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~70 letters] Ad quem locum ista notat Græcus Demosthenis Interpres Ulpianus. [illegible, ~190 letters] Sed in nomine mensis error est calami. Mense enim undecimo rationes suas referebant Arbitri. Ulpianus: [illegible, ~40 letters] Lege [illegible, ~20 letters] Thargelione igitur, qui undecimus erat anni mensis rationes reddebant Arbitri, & quæ postrema erat in negotio [illegible, ~12 letters], ultima quoque erat mensis Thargelionis: nam rationes suas referebant [illegible, ~30 letters]. Dixit autem Demosthenes, [illegible, ~45 letters] eandem diem esse Thargelionis, aut Scirrhophorionis. Erat scilicet [illegible, ~10 letters] Thargelionis, quæ cum sit [illegible, ~8 letters] etiam ad sequentis mensis Pyanepsionis portinet. Optime Ulpianus, si [illegible, ~30 letters] Scirrhophorionis, [illegible, ~8 letters] Thargelionis substituas. [illegible, ~50 letters] [illegible, ~45 letters] [illegible, ~50 letters] μιλῶα.

Fuit præterea bona viri Arbitrium. de quo Iureconsulti, itemque Aristoteles Lib. I. Rhet. cap. XIII. [illegible, ~50 letters] [illegible, ~35 letters] Non igitur hi Arbitri [illegible, ~20 letters], sed ex æquo & bono pronunciabant.
main_text.head: DE IUREIURANDO.
TITULUS SEXTUS.
main_text.p: MAXIMUM remedium, ut loquitur Gaius Lib. V. ad Edictum Pro-vinciale, expediendarum litium in usum venit Iurisiurandi religio, quia ex pactione ipsorum litigatorum decidantur controversia. Leg. I. D. de iureiurando.

page.notes: The Greek text is too faint in the scan to read letter by letter, so every Greek passage is marked illegible with an estimated letter count. Latin in the commentary was read as printed. "portinet" is printed as such (probably for pertinet); left as printed. The initial M of the closing paragraph is a large decorative letter, joined to "MAXIMUM" in the transcription. The ornament rule above "DE IUREIURANDO." is not text and is left out.
